terms.comment: A trampoline in our family vocabulary. The ancient word names an acrobatic apparatus; its precise ancient construction is debated. Leo Latinus uses it for the modern trampoline. This modern sense is not a claim that Romans had modern trampolines.

sources: Leo Latinus, Epistula Leonina 267: petaurum sive resultāculum · Lewis & Short: petaurum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 397 (dēsultōrium).
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
